page.layout: One printed page (left-hand page of the opening, verse text in one column). Running head at top centre. Faint show-through from the facing page in the right margin and a manuscript mark on the left edge; not transcribed. A small catchword-like "Aft" appears at the lower right of the text block, read as the start of the next line, so it is given as a line of verse.

p.i: Alexander vetuit se pingi nisi ab Apelle. Fœlix qui gloriæ Dei celebrandæ operam dat.

main_text.p:
Se pingi vetuit rex Macedo, nisi
Coi pingeret hunc artificis manus,
Qua pingente Venus pulchrior extitit.

An vero sibi plus rex decoris tulit,
Cunctis præpositæ quàm manui dedit?
Est pictor variis auctus honoribus:
At cepit iuuenis rex minimum decus.

Sic tu, summe Pater, dum petis vt fonis
Te sanctum celebrem quotidie meis,
Nil hinc consequeris: quin tua detero
Stridenti calamo facta perennia,
Nullis ingenij dum cano viribus.

At me, me nihili, me nihili lutum
Circumdas vario lumine gloriæ,
Dum vis vt mea vox & comes huic manus
Te sanctum resonet laudibus editis.

O me cœlicolûm cœtibus additum,
Dum cantare Deum te studeo meum!

Non ingrata, precor, sint mea carmina:
Quamuis exiguo fonte cadentia,
Quæ mens officij fert studiosior.
main_text.head: Hymnus Ϲϑμιχτος Deo O. M. Ad Psalmum 148.
main_text.p:
Euphratæ lati, rapidíque ad Tygridis vndas,
Finibus à patrijs Israel exul erat.
Hic Solymæ templo, dum staret, cantica nota
Imperio iussus dicere barbarico,
Abnuit. Ecquis enim, cœlóque soloque nefando,
Auribus impuris carmina sacra daret?

page.notes: The left margin carries a large decorative engraving and faint marginal text that is not legible; not transcribed. Several words in the right margin are show-through from the facing page. The "Ϲϑμιχτος" Greek heading is a damaged reading of the printed Greek word and is uncertain.
